family.name: Operations Manager
family.summary: One warehouse keeps missing dispatch deadlines and festival week is ten days away: find the real bottleneck (not headcount), plan for the spike, and fix a staffing plan built on wrong assumptions.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Why is one site always late?
stages.summary: Find the real bottleneck at the late site: a late inbound truck that shortens pick time, not too few people. Think aloud.

stages.title: Festival week plan
stages.summary: Choose a plan for a big order spike in ten days. Tests capacity planning and cost. Think aloud.

stages.title: Festival week, day two
stages.summary: What their plan led to. Tests adapting under pressure.

stages.title: Check the staffing plan
stages.summary: A staffing plan that uses the best site's speed everywhere, ignores breaks and absence, and counts temps as experienced. Think aloud.

stages.title: The shift brief (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the festival-week brief for site supervisors with AI. Catches generic advice and invented numbers.

stages.title: A process you fixed
stages.summary: A real operational problem they fixed. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You run fulfilment for **Toybox**, an online toy store, across three warehouses. Orders must leave the warehouse by 6 pm on the day they're placed (before 2 pm). Each picker shift is 8 hours; most of the work happens after the inbound truck is unloaded.
Your boss says: "Kundli is always late. It probably needs more people." Festival week starts in **10 days**, when orders usually jump about **70%** for a week.
Temporary pickers cost ₹1,000 a day each and pick at about 65% of an experienced picker's speed.
The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Tell us about a time you made something run faster or smoother.
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

stages.title: Why is one site always late?

prompt.text: **Why does Kundli miss its dispatch deadline?** Is your boss right that it needs more people? Use the numbers.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Hire temporary pickers at all three sites
Move the late site’s inbound truck to the morning, then add temps where still short
Cap orders at the late site and send the rest to the other two
Extend shifts with overtime at all sites

prompt.text: Orders will be about 70% higher for festival week. **What is your plan?** Pick one, size it with numbers (people, cost, capacity), and say what could go wrong.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Hire temporary pickers at all three sites"

prompt.text: The temps arrived, but Kundli still dispatched only 74% on time: the extra people stood around until the 11:00 truck arrived, then got in each other's way.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Move the late site’s inbound truck to the morning, then add temps where still short"

prompt.text: The truck now arrives at 7:00 and on-time dispatch at Kundli is up. But the transporter says the early slot costs 15% more, and Finance wasn't told.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Cap orders at the late site and send the rest to the other two"

prompt.text: Rerouted orders arrive a day later than promised, and customer complaints about delivery dates have tripled. The other two sites are now at 88% on time.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Extend shifts with overtime at all sites"

prompt.text: On day two, picking errors are up 4x and 9 pickers at Kundli called in sick. The site supervisor says the team is exhausted.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: A supervisor drafted the festival staffing plan below. **Find the wrong assumptions, worst first, and say how much each one throws the plan off.**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: Every picker, permanent or temporary, picks 13 orders an hour (our best week ever).
Each picker works 8 productive hours a day.
Everyone on the roster turns up.
Temps start on the first day of festival week; training happens on the job.
Plan is reviewed every evening with each site supervisor.

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.

Write the one-page brief for the three site supervisors for festival week (under 200 words): the daily targets per site, the shift plan, what to escalate and when, and the one thing that matters most.

items: Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about an operational process you fixed, and how you knew it was broken.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
